newsitem.title: USA: Judge declares mistrial in Orange County trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge declares mistrial in Orange County trial.

text.p: The first criminal trial related to the bankruptcy of Orange County, Calif., ended in a mistrial Friday after the jury was unable to reach a verdict.
Superior Court Judge J. Stephen Czuleger declared a mistrial in the case of former Orange County Budget Director Ronald Rubino.
Rubino, 44, was indicted by a county grand jury in December 1995 for allegedly aiding former county Treasurer Robert Citron in diverting funds from other government agencies for the county's benefit.
Jurors told the judge Friday that they were deadlocked. The foreman of the panel said jurors were split 9-to-3 in favour of acquittal. They had been deliberating since Sept. 4.
Rubino's criminal trial is the first arising from the Orange County bankruptcy, the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.

Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.
